inputs.name: DevicePairingService.constructor.options
inputs.description: Optional transport override: its fetch replaces the global fetch for every relay call this service makes, and the default {} uses the global fetch. It is read on each call, and every relay request is sent with redirect set to error, so a redirect rejects that call.

inputs.name: DevicePairingService.poll.pending
inputs.description: The PendingPairing that request returned: poll builds the relay path from its origin, input.hostId and input.pairingId and posts an empty JSON object, so none of its key material is sent.

inputs.name: DevicePairingService.exchange.pending
inputs.description: The PendingPairing that request returned: exchange posts its verifier to the relay, opens the sealed approval with approvalKey, and requires the relay's deviceId and the approval's deviceId to equal this pending deviceId. It builds the returned DeviceCredentials from origin, input.hostId, hostKey, deviceId and keys, with the relay's credential and the approval's hostName, generation and grant.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.scanned
outputs.description: Resolves to the PendingPairing that request builds from the offer read from the scanned text and the device, and rejects when the text is refused or the request fails.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.request
outputs.description: Resolves once the relay answers the request with OK, to a PendingPairing holding the input, the checked origin, the device keys, the relay's hostKey, the deviceId, the verifier whose challenge was sent, and the approval key.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.poll
outputs.description: Resolves to the state the relay reports for the pairing: 'open', 'requested', 'approved', 'denied' or 'expired'. The value is passed through without a check, and a relay answer that is not OK rejects instead.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.exchange
outputs.description: Resolves to the DeviceCredentials of the approved device: its origin, hostId, hostKey, hostName, deviceId, the relay credential, the device keys in stored form, and the approval's generation and grant.

errors.name: DevicePairingError
errors.description: The Error that each operation rejects with, whose message names the failed check: 'offer-invalid', 'offer-unsupported', 'offer-environment' or 'offer-expired' for a refused scanned text; 'Check the pairing details and try again.' for input that fails the checks; 'The relay did not present the key of this computer.' when the relay's hostKey is missing or does not derive hostId; 'The approval is not for this device.' when the approval names another device; and 'The pairing was refused or has expired.' when a relay answer is not OK. Errors from fetch, response parsing and the crypto helpers are not caught and propagate unchanged.

inputs.name: DevicePairingService.poll.pending
inputs.description: The PendingPairing that request returned: poll builds the relay path from its origin, input.hostId and input.pairingId and posts an empty JSON object, so none of its key material is sent.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.poll
outputs.description: Resolves to the state the relay reports for the pairing: 'open', 'requested', 'approved', 'denied' or 'expired'. The value is passed through without a check, and a relay answer that is not OK rejects instead.

errors.name: DevicePairingError
errors.description: Rejects with 'The pairing was refused or has expired.' when the relay's answer to the poll is not OK. Errors from fetch and response parsing propagate unchanged.

inputs.name: DevicePairingService.exchange.pending
inputs.description: The PendingPairing that request returned: exchange posts its verifier to the relay, opens the sealed approval with approvalKey, and requires the relay's deviceId and the approval's deviceId to equal this pending deviceId. It builds the returned DeviceCredentials from origin, input.hostId, hostKey, deviceId and keys, with the relay's credential and the approval's hostName, generation and grant.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.exchange
outputs.description: Resolves to the DeviceCredentials of the approved device: its origin, hostId, hostKey, hostName, deviceId, the relay credential, the device keys in stored form, and the approval's generation and grant.

errors.name: DevicePairingError
errors.description: Rejects with 'The pairing was refused or has expired.' when the relay's answer to the exchange is not OK, and with 'The approval is not for this device.' when the relay's or the approval's deviceId differs from the pending deviceId or the credential is not 43 base64url characters. A sealed approval that does not open with approvalKey also rejects, from openPairing.

inputs.name: DevicePairingService.constructor.options
inputs.description: Optional transport override: its fetch replaces the global fetch for every relay call this service makes, and the default {} uses the global fetch. It is read on each call, and every relay request is sent with redirect set to error, so a redirect rejects that call.

outputs.name: DevicePairingService.constructor
outputs.description: The DevicePairingService instance that the constructor creates, which keeps options so that every later call uses options.fetch when one is given.
